text:
Noah Patel: FYI Helios Insurance requested a perf validation for a POC. Target is 4k sustained QPS for short claim summaries, with occasional 20s morning bursts. SLO: p95 < 220ms for <=140 tokens. Need run plan + 1mo/12mo committed pricing by EOD.

Sofia Martinez: Quick clarifiers: is 4k QPS all gen or mixed with embedding/search? And any encryption/BYOK requirements noted?

Noah Patel: Buyer says ~92% generation, 6% embeddings, 2% analytics calls. They flagged that keys must be customer-managed but didn't insist on HSM yet.

Kai Huang: Proposed load profile: 12m total: 8m ramp to 4k (gentle), 30m sustain (for long window), during sustain inject 3x 20s bursts at +150% spaced ~7m apart, then cool-down. Capture p50/p90/p95/p99, error-rate, CPU/GPU heatmaps, and tail-latency CDF. Also record token/sec and tokens per request.

Kai Huang: Example runner snippet (pseudo):

```
# pseudo k6/vegeta hybrid
load-run --url https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/generate \
  --stages "8m:4000,30m:4000,5m:0" \
  --spikes "20s:+150%@7m,20s:+150%@14m,20s:+150%@21m" \
  --body sample_claims.json --hdr "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --report artifacts/helios-5067890123
```

Ops SRE: For repeatability we should pin model hash and disable async background warmup. If they keep BYOK but not HSM, Dedicated can support CMK via KMS proxy. Private only if they require HSM. Also recommend routing embeddings to a separate pool to avoid KV cache fragmentation.

Security Team: I'll draft the security answers: residency, CMK support, SOC2/ISO attachments, and log forwarding. Ask buyer if SIEM requires syslog or HTTPS ingestion.

Sofia Martinez: Pricing request: procurement wants 1-month and 12-month committed options, plus hosted on-demand numbers. Include burst credit pricing and overage per-token. Also show rough GPU-pool sizing rationale.

Kai Huang: Back-of-envelope tokens: avg 120 prompt + 100 completion ~220 tokens per req. 4k * 220 = 880k tokens/s. For an open 30B FP16 we estimate ~4-6 A100-eq; 4-bit quant might be 3-4. Long story: I'll run a sim to refine.

perf-bot: scheduled job helios-poc-5067892000 (runner perf-grid-4).

Noah Patel: Buyer also asked about multi-AZ failover during the spike scenario and whether we can guarantee tail SLOs. We'll include recommended multi-AZ routing and expected failover latency.

Ops SRE: Runbook notes: reserve stage Dedicated min=3 max=8; pre-warm cache; set autoscale fast-path for bursts; set alert p95 > 300ms and error-rate > 0.4%. If we see KV thrash, isolate embeddings.

Kai Huang: I'll run two sims tonight: mixed traffic and gen-only. ETA: results posted by 8:30am PT tomorrow with GPU-seconds and heatmaps.

Sofia Martinez: Once Kai posts numbers I'll draft the two-tier quote and a short rationale doc: Dedicated vs Hosted for burst handling, including cost sensitivity. Ravi from finance will review.

Security Team: Also flag to buyer: if they want SIEM integration, we'll need their ingest endpoint and retention policy. For CMK we need onboarding steps.

Noah Patel: I'll set a short 30min sync with Helios for tomorrow 9:30am PT to walk plan and confirm SIEM/keys. Invite will include Ops and Security.

perf-bot: run started helios-poc-5067892000 (job id 7742). ETA ~45m.

Kai Huang: Starting sim now. Will capture per-route traces and attach sample prompts.

Ops SRE: FYI if autoscale goes to max during bursts monitor for p99 spikes; add temporary circuit-breaker if error-rate climbs.

Sofia Martinez: Summary actions:
- Kai: sims + GPU sizing (deliver by 8:30am PT)
- Ops SRE: reserve pool + runbook (EOD)
- Security Team: draft security answers + SIEM integration checklist (EOD)
- Noah: buyer sync invite + questionnaire attach

Noah Patel: Thanks team 680. Any blockers?

Kai Huang: None, kicking off now.

perf-bot: run complete helios-poc-5067892000 (artifacts: helios-5067890123.tar.gz).
